The first release of Janitor for Payload 3. Janitor compares your storage with your database. It reports orphaned files, missing files and unused documents, and it deletes only what an admin approves. For Payload 4, use the `beta` tag (1.x).

```bash
pnpm add @seshuk/payload-plugin-janitor
```

Requires Payload 3.83 or later and Node.js 22 or later. Run `payload generate:importmap` after you add the plugin. Setup and every option are in the [README](https://github.com/maximseshuk/payload-plugin-janitor/tree/0.x#readme).

**Highlights**

- `orphans`, `missing` and `unused` checks for upload and ordinary collections. References come from the database itself. When the plugin is unsure, it counts a document as used.
- A scan only writes findings. A purge deletes only the findings an admin marked `delete`, and it checks each one again right before it deletes it.
- A usage panel on the edit view and a delete guard.
- Storage adapters for S3, R2, Google Cloud Storage, Azure, Bunny, uploadthing, Vercel Blob and local disk.
- Runs inside the request, as a Payload job or on a cron.
